submission.justification: Simulated 100 GeV electron resolution (100k events each): F1 gives 3.81/3.25/4.44% at 2/5/10 mm; F2 gives 4.66/4.03/5.38%; F3 gives 5.72/5.22/7.04%. F1 at 5 mm is the best resolution, but the hard residual-dose requirement (<=20 uSv/h at 1 m after one week cooldown) cannot be verified from the project materials: candidate_specs.md gives only qualitative descriptions ("dense alloy with a short radiation length", "standard structural absorber"), and the simulation tool returns only resolution. Dense heavy alloys can carry activation-prone impurities, so F1 carries unverified dose risk. I therefore recommend F3 at 5 mm as the conservative choice under the hard constraint: it is the standard structural absorber, most likely to have low activation, and 5 mm is its best-resolution thickness (5.2%). This costs about 2 percentage points of resolution relative to F1. The dose compliance of F3 is also unverified and must be confirmed with an activation calculation before the choice is final. If F1 is shown to meet the dose limit at 5 mm, it would be the better option for resolution.

requirements.requirement: Best possible energy resolution at 100 GeV
requirements.evidence: Best simulated resolution is F1 at 5 mm (3.25%). The recommended F3 at 5 mm gives 5.22%, a deliberate trade-off against the hard dose constraint.
